full_judgment:
The entire 23.13 acre 'Ka' schedule suit land of Title Suit No. 23 of 2008 appertaining to C.S. khatian No. 07 of Mouza Chandona being projabili property under the previous Bhawal Jaminder. Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury and others represented by court of words. the then government for the purpose of acquisition of rent receiving interest of the said jaminder, at first, published projabili property gazette notification under section 3 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, shortly SAT-Act, 1950 on 24.03.1952 (Exhibit 7), describing therein the schedules of projabili properties and thereafter, the government after paying compensation to the said jaminder for acquisition of rent receiving interest of their projabili property cited in the said projabili gazette, published compensation payment gazetee on 29.02.1956 (Exhibit-9) declaring compensation had been paid to the jaminders as per compensation, when the Government prepared and published S.A. khatian No. 63 (Exhibit-1) connecting with the suit property was duly prepared and published in the names of the previous joint projas, Chan Miah and Basaruddin in equal /8/ (eight) annas share; after scrutinizing the concerned projabili property papers and documents connected with the suit property remained in the sherestha/ custody of the jaminder and thereafter, the Revenue Department of the Government, like title register of the then jaminder, Kumar Rabindra Narayan Roy Chowdhury represented by Court of Wards (Exhibit-4), projabili property gazette (Exhibit-9) etc. upgrading their status from projas to owners. The government not only prepared and published S.A. khatian No. 63 (Exhibit-1) in the names of the previous projas, Chan Miah and Basaruddin as equal /8/ (eight) annas owners upgrading their status as owners but also inserted their names in the Register-II, Talab Baki Register (Exhibit-5), as rent payees in equal shares to the Government Revenue Department. Further case of them is that, on amicable partition Basaruddin got in total 5.40 acre 'Kha' schedule 6 piece properties in his /8/ (eight) annas share. wherein he and thereafter on his demised, the present plaintiffs appellants petitioners as his heirs have been owning, and possessing by erecting and constructing homestead in the 'Kha (2 )' schedule suit property and by opening holding No. 220, Laxmipura, under Gazipur Municipality against it and by paying taxes and deferent bills like electricity, Titas Gas etc. taken against the said holding No. 220 (exhibit-13 series) and the rest 'Kha( I)', 'Kha(3)', 'Kha(4)', 'Kha (5)', and 'Kha (6)', schedules as agricultural lands and ponds by way of cultivating and by rearing fish; inspite of acquisition of ownership and possession as stated herein above by operation of SAT Act. 1950 in the 'Kha' schedule 6 piece properties, the opposite party No. 1, Mr. Abdur Rouf claining himself as manager of Court of Wards, the defendant. No. 14 of Title Suit No. 23 of 2008 and also claiming as shebayet of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraha, defendant No. 1 of said title suit No. 23 of 2008, opposite party No.2 and 3 of the present petition, came to `Kha' schedule suit properties on 12.12.2007 and expressed to the petitioners that family deity Madhab Bigraha, the defendant No.. 1 through his representation as shebayet, got a decree of declaration of title and recovery of khan possession of total 18.73 acres land out of 'Ka' scheduled 23.13 acres land including the petitioner's 'Kha' scheduled 6 piece 5.40 acres properties in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Gazipur against some third parties, Chan Miah and others and asked the petitioners to handover possession of the said 'Kha' scheduled 6 pieces properties in favour of decree holder, Sree Sree Madhab Bigraha, through him as shebayet; that the petitioners after knowing about the aforesaid decree passed in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985, filed Title Suit No. 23 of 2008 challenging the said decree as fraudulent, collusive and not binding upon them along with other consequential reliefs of confirmation of possession and permanent injunction on 06.01.2008. 

 5. In the said suit the petitioners as plaintiffs filed an application under Order XXXIX Rule 1 and 2 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for ad-interim and temporary injunction on the next day on 07.01.2008 praying for restraining defendant No. 1, Madhab Bigraha and defendant No. 14, Court of Words, Bhawal Raj Estate stating the self same facts of acquisition of title and possession by operation SAT Act. 1950, as stated in the plaint. 

 1. Abdur Rouf, Manager, Bhwal Raj Court of Words Estate of 141-143 Motijheel Commercial Area, P.S. Motijheel, District-Dhaka. 2. Sree Sree Madhab represented by Manager Abdur Rouf Bhwal Raj Court of Wards Estate P.S. Joydebpur, District-Gazipur. 3. Court of Words; Bhwal Raj Estate, represented by its Manager Abdur Rouf of 141-143 Motijheel Commercial Area, P.S. Motijheel, District-Dhaka. 4. Md. Sabbir Hossain. Assistant Manager Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate P.S. Joydebpur, District-Gazipur. 5. Monirul Islam, Chairman Land Reforms Board of 141 -143 Motijheel Commercial Area, P.S. Motijheel, District -Dhaka. 6. Syed Mizanur Rahman, Deputy Commissioner Gazipur -District, District-Gazipur. 7. A lamgir Alam Superintendent of Police Gazipur-District, District-Gazipur. 8. Md. Shahjalal Assistant Commissioner/ Magistrate Gazipur,District, District-Gazipur. 9. Md. Mizanur Rahman Officer-in-charge Joydebpur Police Station Thana- Joydebpur, District-Gazipur. 10. Pabitra Kumar Shaha Anser Adjutant, Gazipur District-Gazipur. 

 11. Opposite party Nos. 1-10 jointly filed counter affidavit by swearing affidavit through opposite party No. 1 Mr. Abdur Roof, who claims himself as shebayet of the opposite party No.2, the deity Sree Sree Madhab Bigraha and Manager of the opposite party No.3, the Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate and also Claimed as Tadbirkar of the other opposite party Nos.4 to 10 who are Government servants stating nothing about his relationship with them though the allegation of violation against each of the opposite parties are distinct and liability thereof are also distinct and several in a violation case. In the said affidavit he stated amongst other that he is conversant with the facts and circumstances with the case as made out in the petition under order 39 rule-(3) of the Code of Civil Procedure. He apart from denying the allegation of violation of injunction order stated amongst other that the present petitioners, Khaliullah and others were not owners of 'Kha(2)' schedule suit properties and also were not in possession thereof and as such, they were not necessary parties in the previous Title suit No. 1219 of 1985. Decree passed in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985 is not a fraudulent decree. Petitioners falsely have initiated Title Suit No. 23 of 2008 and filed the application for temporary injunction upon false statements. He further stated that he did not influence the Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur for sending Executive Magistrate, opposite party No. 8 on 2 8.02.2008 for eviction of the petitioners and the news published in the local News papers about the incidents of 28.02.2008 and also the contents of the G.D. entry No. 142 dated 02.03.2008 are false. He further stated that the petitioners were being not in possession of 'Kha(2)' schedule suit property question of eviction on 03.03.2008 and 05.03.2008 does not arise at all. So, the opposite parties have not violated the injunction order in taking over possession of 'Kha.(2) schedule suit property. Opposite, party No. 9 and 10 having not been added as party in Title Suit No. 23 of 2008, they were not necessary parties in the present violation rule and have been impleaded only to harass them; the Court of Wards being a local authority requested opposite party No. 6. Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur for evicting the illegal occupants of 'Kha(2)' schedule suit properties under the provision of Government and Local Authority. Land and buildings Recovery Act, 1970. Accordingly, the Executive Magistrate, Mollika Khutun evicted the illegal occupiers from 'Kha(2)' schedule suit property on 03.03.2008 at 9 P.M. to 11.40 A.M. as per order of eviction issued by the respondent No. 6, Mr. Syed Mizanur Rahman, the then Deputy Commissioner of Gazipur, passed in Eviction Case No. 3 of 2006 started under Government and Local Authority (Land and building) Recovery Act, 1970 and now the Bhawal Raj Estate is in legal possession of the suit property; against the order of injunction passed in Civil Rule No. 132 (F.M)/ 2008 opposite party Nos. 1, 2 and 3 preferred Civil Miscellaneous Petition for leave to appeal No. 228 of 2008 before the Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court for staying operation of the order of injunction dated 03.03.2008 and got an order of stay on 16.03.2008 and thereafter filed Civil Petition for Leave to appeal No. 680 of 2008 in which stay' order granted earlier has been extended till its disposal. 

 12. Against the counter affidavit filed by opposite party No. 1 to 10, the petitioner, Abul Kalam alias Khaliullah and others filed affidavit in reply stating amongst others that the story of eviction at 9.00 A.M. to 11.45 P.M with the help of Police force on 03.03.2008 are not correct and further stated that the deity being a private artificial person has got no authority to evict the petitioners from their homestead on 03.03.2008 in presence of Advocate. Mrs. Toslima Momin Lima and on 05.03.2008 in presence of said Advocate, Toslima Momin Lima and other 3 Advocates who also sworn affidavit on 10.06.2008 narrating the facts of eviction happened in their presence. They also stated that the facts of eviction of women members from the rest of the two room dated 05.03.2008 were taken place in their presence and the cameraman of Baishakhi Television had taken live pictures thereof and broadcasted in its next clays news on 06.03.2008 at 4.45 P.M. Advocate Mrs. Taslima Momin Lima sworn an affidavit on 04.06.2008 and learned Advocate, Mr. Khandaker Quamrul Hasan (Ripon), Advocates, Ataur Rahman and Sayed Md. Abu Fazal have jointly sworned another affidavit on 10.06.2008 narrating the facts of eviction held on 05.03.2008 in their presence stating that inspite of showing certified copy of the injunction order passed by this Court the opposite party Nos. 1 to 9 evicted the female members of the petitioners from `Kha'(2)1 schedule suit properties and thereafter arrested female member therefrom by starting Criminal Case against them. Opposite party Nos. 1 to 10 though denied the facts stated in the affidavits of aforesaid 4 learned Advocates, but had not made any positive statements against their statements of facts. 

 14. Upon considering the aforesaid facts stated in the violation petition, counter affidavit and affidavit in reply this court framed the following issues: 

 17. Mr. Nurul Amin, learned Advocate of the opposite party Nos. 1 to 10 at the very outset raised a question of maintainability of the violation rule submitting that the order of injunction dated 03.02.2008 was passed only against two legal persons namely, the opposite party No.2, deity. Madhap bigraha (who was defendant No. 1 in the Title No. 23 of 2008) and against opposite party No. 3, Court of Wards,(who was defendant No. 14 in Title Suit No.23 of 2008) and not against other persons. So, impleading other living persons, like opposite party no.1, Abdur Rouf, Manager of Bhawal Raj Estate. opposite party No. 4, Md. Sabbir Hossain, Assistant Manager, Bhawal Court of 'Wards, opposite party No.5. Mr. Monirul Islam, the then Chairman. Land Reform Board cannot be blamed and punished for working for and on behalf of the aforesaid two legal persons even if the alleged eviction is proved by violating the order of injunction dated 03.03.2008 Learned Advocate Mr. Nurul Amin further submitted that the other opposite parties Nos. 6 to 10 being not party in the Title Suit No. 23 of 2008, they also cannot be punished for violation of the order of injunction dated 03.03.2008, passed by the High Court Division. 

 22. Apart from the aforesaid oral evidence, all the P.W.S. stated in one voice that the petitioners were in possession of `Kha(2)1 schedule suit property before their eviction on 03.03.2008 and 05.03.2008. The learned Advocate of the defendant opposite party No. 2 and 3 could not produce anything contrary to those statements by way of cross examinations. 

 So, on consideration of the admitted statements of DW-1, and statement of P.W.S, we are of the view that the petitioners were in possession of the 'kha(2)' schedule suit property before their eviction on 03.03.2008. 

 23. Now, the second question, whether the opposite party No.1 to 10 had evicted the petitioners with the knowledge of the order of injunction as alleged by them. It is alleged by the opposite parties No. 1 to 10 that they had evicted the petitioners on 03.03.2008 in between 9.00 A.M. to 11.45 A.M before reaching the order of injunction to them. On the other hand, the plaintiff-petitioners stated that the injunction order was passed by the Division Bench of the Hon'ble High Court Division consisting of their Lordships Mr. Justice M.A Wahab Miah and Mr. Afzal' Hossain Ahmed, on 03.03.2008 at 11.45 A.M. and their learned Advocate Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman, sent the said order of injunction to fax No. 9252751 to learned Advocate of Gazipur Bar, Mrs. Toslima Momin Lima at 1.30 P.M who after receiving the said fax rushed to 'kha(2)' schedule suit property within 10 minutes and was waiting for showing the same to the opposite parties who went to the suit property at 2.00 P.M. for eviction. Mrs Lima, Advocate, though showed the said order of injunction sent through fax but the opposite party No. 9, Mr. Mizanur Rahman, O.C. Gazipur and opposite party No. 8, Mr. Shahajalal Executive Magistrate, Gazipur, engaged in the eviction case started eviction of the petitioners and their tenants in `kha(2)'schedule suit property violating the order of injunction. The petitioners for proving the aforesaid facts, knowledge of injunction of the opposite parties, annexed several documentary evidences as annexures with the violation petition. From annexure-C it reveals the order of injunction was sent by fax to the fax of the Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur, bearing No. 9261899 on 04.03.2008 and it reveals from annexure-C (1) that the opposite party No. 9, 0.C,. Jaydebpur, was informed about the order of injunction vide G.D No.235 dated 04.03.2008 and the S.P, Gazipur was informed to his fax No.9252167 on 04.03.2008 Moreover, the order of injunction was also served by special messenger on 04.03.2008 upon the opposite party No.2 and 3. The opposite party No. 1 to 10 in their affidavit though vaguely denied of receiving such fax but did not deny that they had no such fax No. 9261899 and 9252167. Since, both the office of S.P and D.C being public office there is no reason of non receiving such fax. Apart from sending the aforesaid fax the news of eviction both on 03.03.2008 and 05.03.2008 published both in local and National News Paper about violating the order of injunction dated 03.03.2008 have neither been denied nor challenged by publishing objection letter. As to the deployment of Ansar by the opposite party No. 10 violating the order of injunction the petitioners specifically stated that they informed about the order of injunction by sending fax to his fax No. 9252129 on 04.03.2008 Annexure C(4) and thereafter on the same date filed an application attaching order of injunction therewith So, it can easily be presumed that the respondent No. 10 had knowledge about the order of injunction. Apart from the aforesaid documentary evidences, the petitioners also proved about the knowledge of order of injunction and its violation by citing 7 witnesses. Out of the aforesaid witnesses, the statements made by Advocate Lima, P.W-4 is very much important. The said witnesses stated in her deposition as follows: 

 24. The aforesaid statements of learned Advocate Mrs. Lima were Corroborated in one voice by the other, P.W.S. i.e. P.W-1, Abul Kalam @ Kaliullah, P.W-2, Akkas Ali, P.W-3  Nazrul Islam, P.W-5 Arifa Khanam and P.W-7, Tahamina Khatun as follows: 

 25. On the other hand, P.W.-2, Akkas Ali, is a contiguous neighbor of 'kha(2)' schedule suit property and a man of 70 years old. He deposed that the rest 2 tin shed ghars remained after eviction of `kha(2)' schedule suit property is being used by Ansar contingent deployed by the opposite party No. 10. He further stated that on 03.03.2008 he was coming back from Rice Research Institute to his house and found that the police contingent are taking preparation to enter in to the house of Abul Kalam @,Kaliullah and others. One women lawyer was prohibiting the police from entering into the houses of Abul Kalam @kaliullah but the police contingent entered into kaliullah's house violating her request and started to demolish the houses leaving only 2-4 ghars. He further stated that on 05.03.2008 they came again with the help of combined force and put the wife of Abu] Kalam and other women in a police van from the remaining, ghars inspite of protest raised by 3 lawyers showing order of injunction of High Court Division. He further stated that except the evicted `kha(2)' .schedule suit property other 5 pieces `kha' schedule properties are yet in position of the plaintiffs, Abul Kalam and others. The said witness was cross examined but no contradictions have been achieved by the contesting defendants. 

 26. PW-3 Nazrul Islam, was a monthly tenant in `kha(2)' schedule suit property and now residing in holding No. 184, Luxmipura. He in his chief stated that there were 14/15 houses in suit holding No-220, Luxmipura. Before eviction he we residing in suit holding No. 220 as monthly tenant. He further stated that he was evicted from the suit holding on 03.03.2008; he further stated that the female members were evicted on 05.03.2008 from the rest of two houses and arrested them when raised objection showing order of injunction. He in cross examination denied the suggestion that the women members were arrested for raising objection in putting barbed fence around `kha(2)' schedule suit property. 

 27. PW-5 Arifa Khanam, who was also a monthly tenant in the `kha(2)'schedule suit property under the plaintiff-petitioners before her eviction therefrom on 03.03.2008 and 05.03.2008. She stated in her deposition that she along with 40 families were monthly tenant in `kha(2)' schedule suit property. There were 15/16 ghars in the said suit property. After demolishing there were 5 ghars remained in the suit property. After demonization there were 5 ghars remained in the Suit property. They came again on 05.03.2008 for further eviction. Two male lawyers and one female lawyer tried to prevent them from evicting her and other women members from the remaining ghars by showing injunction order but the women police forcefully take them out from the house and put into police van for taking to concern police station from 'kha(2)' schedule suit property. This witness was cross examined but without any contradiction of her statements made in her chief examination. 

 28. P. W-6, Mr. Mahbub. Advocate. is a survey knowing Advocate commissioner. He proved his report and exhibited the same as x series. In his report he stated specifically that in the two rooms in 'kha(2)' schedule suit property is now in occupation of Ansars contingent deployed by the opposite party No. 10 and are protecting 'kha(2)' schedule suit property for and on behalf of Court of Wards. He in his report further stated that he noticed the sign and symptom of demolished structures in kha(2)' schedule suit property. The said witness was cross examined but no contradiction of his statement made in his chief. 

 29. PW-7, Tahmina, is wife of plaintiff and PW-1. She stated that she was married in the year 1991 and since then she was residing in suit holding No. 220, poschim Lexmipura till evicted therefrom on 05.02.2008 along with other 40 families. She further stated that there were sixteen ghars in `kha(2)' schedule property and 40 families were residing therein. Those ghars were erected by her father-in-law, Basiruddin. She further stated that on 03.03.2008 when the people of Court of Wards came to the suit property `Kha(2)' schedule at about 1.30 P.M. property, their engaged female lawyer by showing injunction order of the High Court Division tried to prevent them from evicting but the police contingent engaged in eviction did not obey the order of injunction and demolished all the structures except the two wherein female members had taken shelter. Thereafter, they again came on 05.03.2008 and evicted the female members therefrom by force and arrested her and 7 others from the aforesaid two tinshed ghars. She further stated that the police released 5 arrested persons from the police station and sent her and another women to the court. 

 She further stated that after 5 days in jail, she was bailed out from the court. The said witness was cross examined by the defendant Court of Wards but no contradiction was found. 

 33. We have scrutinized the said section and found that the section is applicable in case of the property remained in charge of the court of wards and if the said property is transferred by the court of wards to some third party by sale, gift or by any other modes of transfer, then for giving delivery of possession of such transferred property to said transferee, the court of wards can exercise such power of eviction as stated. Section 18(A) was inserted in the Court of Wards Act after SAT Act. 1950, stating that, the court of wards can keep in its charge only the retainable khas land after acquisitioning rent receiving interest of the rent receiver over its projabili property by the Government under SAT Act, 1950. The petitioners property appertaining to C.S Khatian No. 7 having found at page 492 of projabill property Gazette, it can never be in-charge of the Court of Wards and claiming title therein by the Court of Wards would be another contempt of court as per judgment of the High Court Division as well as Appellate Division of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Bangladesh. It may be further stated that in its written statements, had never claimed suit property appertaining to C.S. khatian No.7 as of its own property, rather claimed as property of private deity of Sree Sree Madhab Bigraha and said Bigraha got decree in Title Suit No. 1219 of 1985, through its so called shebayet Abdur Rod, the Manager, Court of Wards, on 24.10.1996 

 34. On the other hand, the Assistant Manager, Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate, Mr.Sabbir Ahmed as D.W- I , in his cross examination at one time stated that the deity is a family deity of the Wards of Court of. Wards and the said deity has no taken any tenancy settlement of the suit land from the Court of Wards and is also not the owner and possessor of the Suit property; rather, the Court of Wards is the owner of the suit property and in another time, he stated that deity is the owner of the suit property. From his said contradictory statements it can easily be concluded that neither the deity nor the Court of Wards was ever owner in possession of the suit property. Since the suit property is cited in the projabili property Gazette, at pa 492 (Ext-5) and from the exhibit-4 title registrar of the jaminder and Ext-5, the register II of the Revenue Department of the Government and other documents like S.A Khatian, C.A Roll etc the name of the petitioners' predecessor Basiruddin is found to have been cited, as proja under the jamindar Bhawal Court of Wards, it can never be owned either by the Wards through Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate as it is barred by section 3(2) of the SAT Act, 1950 and 8(A) of the Court of Wards Act 1879 and also by P.O 90 of 1972 or by the deity as its own property. Moreover, the system of management and administration of the property of the deity and that of the Court of Wards are distinct and different to each other, as the first. one is managed and administered as per Endowment Act, 1863 and second one is managed and administered by Court of Wards Act, 1879 as of private person's property. So, in no circumstances the Government Property Recovery Act, 1970 can be applicable in case of the kha(2)' schedule suit property. So, starting of eviction case No.03/06 under the Government property recovery Act, 1970 and evicted the petitioners from their 'kha(2)' schedule private property by using Government machineries is beyond the jurisdiction of Court of Wards and also of the Deputy Commissioner of Gazipur. 

 35. The Learned Advocate of the petitioners, Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman submitted that during the pendency of this rule the Court of Wards Bhawal Raj Estate had changed their views in claiming their title over its projabili property as cited in the Projabili property Gazette published on 24.03.1952 by the Government under section 3(A) of the SAT Act 1950. following the decisions, observations  and directions of the Hon'ble Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh reported in 31 DLR (S/C) page -13, 53 and 14 MLR (A/D) page - 40 and also the judgment passed in writ petition No. 17056 and 17216 of 2012 by the High Court Division. He further submitted that the Court of Wards had already given under takings in Contempt Petition No.226 of 2013 and 346 of 2013 to the effect that they would not make any further claim over its projabili property cited in the projabili property Gazette in future and also begged apology for making such claim over the projabili property. Their Lordships Mr. Justice Mr. Miza Hossain Haider and Mr. Khurshed Adam Sarker in their judgment dated 10.02.2014 though accepted their apology but had given warning to the Court of Wards not to claim over its projabili properties cited in the projabili property Gazette in future. The petitioner's property appertaining to C.S khatian No.7 of Mouza Chandona, being cited at page 492 of said projabili property Gazette (Exhibit-7) the petitioners filed an application on 18.02.2014 before us for knowing the view of the present Chairman, Land Reform Board in respect of Court of Wards' projabili properties, upon whom the Management and administration of the court of Wards has been bestowed by the Government. But on the vehement protest raised by Mr. Nurul Amin, Advocate, his view could not be ascertained. So, we have been compelled to take up the violation rule for hearing and heard for days together. 

 36. After lengthy hearing the rule and after going through the evidences both documentary and oral from the paper Book of Appeal from Original Decree No 128 of 2012 and also from the violation petition and counter affidavit and also the affidavit in reply. of the parties as stated herein above, we have already come to the conclusion that the petitioners have successfully proved their case without any doubt that the opposite party nos. 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 are directly involved in evicting the petitioners on 03.03.2008 and 05.03.2008 from their homestead 'kha(2)' schedule suit property, violating the order of injunction dated 03.03.2008, as such they are liable to pay total Tk.1.00(one crore) as claimed by the petitioners in their legal notice dated 04.03.2008 (annexure-D) as compensation to the petitioners as damages caused by demolishing their pucca and semi pucca structures of the `kha(2)' schedule suit property and also are liable to be punished for evicting the petitioners therefrom violating the order of injunction and for keeping the remaining two tin sheds houses of the petitioners in their illegal possession through Ansers deployed by the opposite party No. 10 violating the order of injunction. 

 reason, particularly in the third world countries, doing justice is now a challenge and some time yield to the executive power of state as absolute power corrupt absolutely. In the case of Rex-Sussex Justice exparte Mecoity, (1924) 1 Q B 256 at page 259, Lord Hewast C.J. laid down the principle "that it is merely of some importance that Justice should not only be done, but should manifestly and undoubtedly be seen to be done. Lord Denning gots further to laid that 'Be you ever so high, law is above you.' Every one shall have to obey law and courts as Court is to implement law failing which 'there would be law and order situation. 

 In cross-examination he stated as: 

 43. We may mentioned that Mr. Khalilur Rahman, learned Advocate supply some photo copies showing the damages caused to the property of plaintiffs along with recorded C.D. showing when breaking was continuing learned Advocate of behalf of the plaintiffs, Mrs. Lima was standing there with the photo copy of order of injunction. Violator Nos. I and 2 are Manager of Bhawal Raj Court of Wards Estate and it is in the evidence that over this property several litigations between plaintiffs and violator Nos. 1 and 2 were filed, as such it can be safely said that violator No. 1 and 2 were aware of the proceeding. It can be said that violators were in know of the proceeding pending before the court, as such after knowing fully of the proceeding pending before the court they either dispossessed the plaintiffs by not executing decree or come before the court and took permission of the court but by sheer disobedience to the Court willfully and intentionally dispossess the plaintiffs to frustrate the Court proceedings. It appears from the papers that violator Nos. 1 and 2 went to Deputy Commissioner straight away who passed the order for evicting the plaintiffs from suit land without there being any executing proceeding for that. It is borne in mind that when any suit or proceeding pending before any court of law unless there be any permission from court nobody on earth can take any step to forestall the decree to be passed and disturn the scemnario on the date of filing of the proceeding where there was any restrained, order or not. If there be any restrain order not supported by the fact, then the litigant must came before the court and after taking permission from court then take step for possession of the suit property. It may be true that then violaters have no knowledge about injunction order dated 03,03.2008 but this violators must have knowledge of the injunction on the day following 03.03.2008 and knowing of the same the violators did not give up possession voluntarily or did not come before the court either for varying or modifying or by setting aside the order of injunction. It appears from 03.03.2008 for the last 6 years violaters possessed the suit property and enjoyed. 

 Mr. Nurul Alam, learned Advocate of the opposite party Nos. 1 to 6 thereafter raised a question of maintainability of the violation rule stating that the order of injunction dated 03.03.2008 was passed only against two legal persons namely, the opposite party No.2, the deity, Madhab Bigraha (who was defendant No. 1 in the title suit No. 23/08) and against the opposite party No.3, Court of Wards, (who was defendant No. 14 in the title suit No. 23/08) and not against other persons. So, impleading of other living persons like opposite party No. 1, Abdur Rouf, Manager of Bhawal Raj Estate, opposite party No.4, Md. Sabbir Hossain, Assistant Manager, Bhawal Court of Wards, opposite party No.5, Mr. Monirul Islam, the then Chairman, Land Reform Board cannot be blamed and punished for working for and on behalf of the aforesaid two legal persons, even if, the alleged eviction is proved by violating the order of injunction dated 03.03.2008. The said learned Advocate Mr. Nurul Amin further submitted that the other opposite party Nos. 6 to 10 being were not party in the main title suit No. 23/08, they also cannot be punished for violation of the order of injunction dated 03.03.2008, passed by the Hon'ble High Court Division. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Khalilur Rahman the learned Advocate of the petitioners submitted that the order of injunction passed against some statutory organization corporation or legal person is binding not only upon the said organization and legal person but also upon its officers. Managers who execute its works for and on behalf of said organization, corporation and legal person as per rule 5 of the order 39 of the Code of Civil procedure. In this respect the petitioners' learned Advocate cited a ruling of the High Court Division of the case of Md. Mobasher hossain and another-VS-M/s. Saidur Rahman (pvt.) Ltd. Reported in 11 BLT (H/C) page 349. 

 48. Now as to the issue No.3 abetting in eviction by the opposite party No.7, the then Sp, Gazipur, the opposite party No.8, the then Executive Magistrate, the opposite party No.9, the then Officer in Charge of Joydebpur Police Station and lastly the opposite party No. 10, the then Ansar Adjutant of Gazipur, the learned Advocate of the petitioners submitted to us that since all of them had helped the opposite party No. 1, Abdur Rouf the then Manager of Court of Wards, the opposite party No.4, the Assistant Manager, Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate, the opposite party No.5, the then Chairman land Reform Board and the opposite party No.6, the then Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur in evicting the petitioners from their homestead violating the order of injunction, they are also liable to be punished for helping in eviction to the opposite parties Nos. 1,4,5 and 6. On the other hand the opposite party No.7 and opposite party No.9 by appearing through their newly appointed advocate submitted fresh and separate counter affidavit stated that they had been compelled to participate in the eviction process with the pressure of their higher authorities. They further stated in their counter affidavit, that on 28.02.2008 they raised objection in evicting petitioners and did not help the opposite parties Nos. 1,4,5 and 6 in evicting the petitioners. But for such non-co-operation they had to face explanation from their higher authorities. At last Mr. Omar Shadat, their learned advocate begged apology and exonerate from the charge of abetment. Similarly, the opposite party No.8 by engaging Mr. Abul Kalam Azad, advocate filed separate counter affidavit stating that he was not assigned in eviction preceding but he was appointed only to see law and order situation in the suit property. On arrival to the 'kha(2)' schedule suit property, he found that, the opposite party No.1. Abdur Rouf is present there with the combined force. He further stated in his counter affidavit that he came back from the suit property as and when he came to know about the order of injunction passed by this High Court Division showing utmost respect thereto. At last, he begged apology and exonerate him from the charge of abetment in violating the order of injunction. On the other hand, the opposite party No. 10 by appearing through his newly appointed advocate Mr. Ashadullab stated that he neither evicted the petitioners nor demolished any structures of the 'kha(2)' schedule suit property. He had only deployed 16 ansars on 06.03.2008 at the request of the District Magistrate on 05.03.2008 without knowing about the order of injunction. 

 50. Now as to the punishment to the opposite part„ No. 1. Abdur Rouf, the manager Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate, it is found that he is the main architect in evicting the petitioners from their homestead. He not only filed title suit No. 1219 of 1985 claiming him as sherayet of the Deity. the opposite party No.2 and got decree against some fictitious persons who were not in possession of the suit property, but when he found that the said decree is in executable against the plaintiffs petitioners, he managed the opposite party No.6 and had evicted the petitioners from their homestead demolishing 14 semi pucca ghars keeping two intact for deploying ansars therein violating the order of injunction. Mr. Rouf as an ex government servant knew well that the provision of Government Property Recovery Act, 1970 could not be applicable either in the property of the Deity or of the Court of Wards. So, in our view, he is liable to be punished and also pay compensation for demolishing of 14 semi pucca ghars. Accordingly he is liable to pay compensation of TK. 1,00,00,000/- (one crore) only as asked by the petitioners in their legal notice dated 04.03.2008 (exhibit-24). As to involvement of the other persons connecting with the court of wards, the opposite party No.4, Assistant manager, Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate and the opposite party No.6, the then Chairman, Land Reform Board, it is found from the evidence, that they have been misleaded by the opposite party No.1, Abdur Rouf, the Manager, Court of Wards, Bhawal Raj Estate. Even that they having found involved in eviction process violating the order of injunction, are also liable to be punished but with lesser punishment. As to the punishment for violation of the order of injunction to the opposite party No.6, the then Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur, it is found that he being a custodian of the public of his district, he has a duty to see and protect the interest of the public under his district. But in this case he has intentionally started eviction case under Act, 1970 for evicting the petitioners from their private property which have no connection whatsoever with the government property. So, he should he awarded an exemplary punishment, so that any other government officials like him do not dare to evict private persons from their private properties taking advantage of his official position as government servant and misusing his official position. 

 51. Hence the Rule is partly made absolute awarding 30 days in civil prison to opposite party No. 6, Syed Mizanur Rahman, the then Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur, 15 days in civil prison and compensation of Tk. 1,00,00,000/- (one crore) only to the opposite party No. 1, Abdur Rouf, Manager Court of Wards for paying to the petitioners as damages of demolishing their 14 semi pucca ghars within one month from the receipt of this judgment and the opposite party No.4. Mr. Sabbir Hossain, the Assistant Manager, court of Wards, Bhawal Raj -Estate and also the opposite party No.5, Monirul Islam, the then Chairman, Land Reform Board are award 5 days in civil prison each. The civil prison would be effected and the compensation would be realized as per provision of Code of Civil procedure. The other abettor opposite parties are hereby exonerated from their respective charges of abetment in evicting the petitioners violating the order of injunction. Considering their statements made in their counter affidavit and also begging pardon to us. No order as to cost.
